[[File:PatrickDehornoy.jpg|thumb|Patrick Dehornoy in 2012]]
In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] area of [[braid theory]], the '''Dehornoy order''' is a left-invariant [[total order]] on the [[braid group]], found by [[Patrick Dehornoy]].<ref>{{citation | last = Dehornoy|first= Patrick|authorlink=Patrick Dehornoy | title = Deux propriétés des groupes de tresses | journal = [[Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I]] | date = 1992 | volume=315 | number = 6 | pages = 633–638 | mr = 1183793 | issn = 0764-4442}}</ref><ref name = Dehornoy94 >{{citation | last = Dehornoy|first= Patrick | title = Braid groups and left distributive operations | journal = [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] | date = 1994 | volume=345 | number = 1 | pages = 115–150 | mr = 1214782 | doi = 10.2307/2154598 |jstor= 2154598 | doi-access = free }}</ref>  Dehornoy's original discovery of the order on the braid group used [[huge cardinal]]s, but there are now several more elementary constructions of it.<ref name = DDRW08>{{citation | last1=Dehornoy | first1=Patrick | last2=Dynnikov | first2=Ivan | last3=Rolfsen | first3=Dale | last4=Wiest | first4=Bert | title=Ordering braids | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=St68wblwRlEC | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | location=Providence, R.I. | series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs | isbn=978-0-8218-4431-1 | mr=2463428 | year=2008 | volume=148}}</ref>

==Definition==
Suppose that <math>\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}</math> are the usual generators of the braid group <math>B_n</math> on <math>n</math> strings. Define a <math>\sigma_i</math>'''-positive word''' to be a braid that admits at least one expression in the elements <math>\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}</math> and their inverses, such that the word contains <math>\sigma_i</math>, but does not contain <math>\sigma_i^{-1}</math> nor <math>\sigma_j^{\pm 1}</math> for <math>j<i</math>.

The set <math>P</math> of positive elements in the Dehornoy order is defined to be the elements that can be written as a <math>\sigma_i</math>-positive word for some <math>i</math>. We have:

* <math>PP \subseteq P;</math> 
* <math>P, \{1\}</math> and <math>P^{-1}</math> are disjoint ("acyclicity property"); 
* the braid group is the union of <math>P, \{1\}</math> and <math>P^{-1}</math> ("comparison property").

These properties imply that if we define <math>a < b</math> as <math>a^{-1}b \in P</math> then we get a left-invariant total order on the braid group. For example, <math>\sigma_1 < \sigma_2 \sigma_1</math> because the braid word <math>\sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1</math> is not <math>\sigma_1</math>-positive, but, by the braid relations, it is equivalent to the <math>\sigma_1</math>-positive word <math>\sigma_2\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1}</math>, which lies in <math>P</math>.

== History ==
[[Set theory]] introduces the hypothetical existence of various "hyper-infinity" notions such as [[large cardinal]]s. In 1989, it was proved that one such notion, axiom <math>I_3</math>, implies the existence of an [[algebraic structure]] called an acyclic shelf which in turn implies the [[Decidability (logic)|decidability]] of the [[Word problem for groups|word problem]] for the left self-distributivity law <math>LD: x(yz)=(xy)(xz),</math> a property that is a priori unconnected with large cardinals.<ref>{{Citation | last1= Dehornoy | first1= Patrick | title= Sur la structure des gerbes libres | journal = Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I | year= 1989  | volume= 309 | issue= 3 | pages= 143–148  | mr= 1005627}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1= Laver| first1= Richard | authorlink1=Richard Laver | title=The left distributive law and the freeness of an algebra of elementary embeddings | journal= [[Advances in Mathematics]] | year=1992 | volume= 91 | issue= 2 | pages= 209–231 | mr = 1149623 | doi = 10.1016/0001-8708(92)90016-E | doi-access=free | hdl= 10338.dmlcz/127389 | hdl-access= free }}</ref>

In 1992, Dehornoy produced an example of an acyclic shelf by introducing a certain [[groupoid]] <math>\mathcal{G}_{LD}</math> that captures the geometrical aspects of the <math>LD</math> law. As a result, an acyclic shelf was constructed on the [[braid group]] <math>B_\infty</math>, which happens to be a quotient of <math>\mathcal{G}_{LD}</math>, and this implies the existence of the braid order directly.<ref name = Dehornoy94/> Since the braid order appears precisely when the large cardinal assumption is eliminated, the link between the braid order and the acyclic shelf was only evident via the original problem from set theory.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Dehornoy | first1=Patrick | title= Another use of set theory | journal= Bulletin of Symbolic Logic | year=1996 | volume= 2 | issue= 4 | pages= 379–391 | doi= 10.2307/421170 | mr=1321290 | jstor=421170 }}</ref>

== Properties ==
* The existence of the order shows that every braid group <math>B_n</math> is an orderable group and that, consequently, the algebras <math>\Z B_n</math> and <math>\C B_n</math> have no zero-divisor.
* For <math>n \geqslant 3</math>, the Dehornoy order is not invariant on the right: we have <math>\sigma_2 < \sigma_1</math> and <math>\sigma_2 \sigma_1 > \sigma_1^2</math>. In fact no order of <math>B_n</math> with <math>n \geqslant 3</math> may be invariant on both sides.
* For <math>n \geqslant 3</math>, the Dehornoy order is neither [[Archimedean property|Archimedean]], nor [[Conrad's property|Conradian]]: there exist braids <math>\beta_1, \beta_2</math> satisfying <math>\beta_1^p < \beta_2</math> for every <math>p</math> (for instance <math>\beta_1 = \sigma_2</math> and <math>\beta_2 = \sigma_1</math>), and braids <math>\beta_1, \beta_2</math> greater than <math>1</math> satisfying <math>\beta_1 > \beta_2 \beta_1^p</math> for every <math>p</math> (for instance, <math>\beta_1 = \sigma_2^{-1} \sigma_1</math> and <math>\beta_2 = \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_1</math>).
* The Dehornoy order is a well-ordering when restricted to the positive braid [[monoid]] <math>B_n^+</math> generated by <math>\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}</math>.<ref>{{citation | last = Laver|first= Richard | title = Braid group actions on left distributive structures, and well orderings in the braid groups | journal = [[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]] | date = 1996 | volume=108 | pages=81–98 | mr = 1382244 | doi=10.1016/0022-4049(95)00147-6 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The [[order type]] of the Dehornoy order restricted to <math>B_n^+</math> is the ordinal <math>\omega^{\omega^{n - 2}}</math>.<ref>{{citation | author = Burckel, Serge | title = The wellordering on positive braids | journal = [[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]] | date = 1997 | volume=120 | number = 1 | pages = 1–17 | mr = 1466094 | doi=10.1016/S0022-4049(96)00072-2 | doi-access = free }}</ref>
* The Dehornoy order is also a well-ordering when restricted to the dual positive braid monoid <math>B_n^{*+}</math> generated by the elements <math>\sigma_i \dots \sigma_{j-1} \sigma_{j} \sigma_{j-1}^{-1}\dots \sigma_i^{-1}</math> with <math>1 \leqslant i < j \leqslant n</math>, and the order type of the Dehornoy order restricted to <math>B_n^{*+}</math> is also <math>\omega^{\omega^{n - 2}}</math>.<ref>{{citation | last = Fromentin | first = Jean | title = Every braid admits a short sigma-definite expression | journal = [[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]] | date = 2011 | volume = 13 | number = 6 | pages = 1591–1631 | doi = 10.4171/JEMS/289 | doi-access = free | mr = 2835325| arxiv = 0811.3902 }}</ref>
* As a [[binary relation]], the Dehornoy order is decidable. The best decision algorithm is based on Dynnikov's tropical formulas,<ref>{{citation | last = Dynnikov | first = Ivan | title = On a Yang-Baxter mapping and the Dehornoy ordering | journal =Russian Mathematical Surveys | date = 2002 | volume = 57 | number = 3 | pages = 151–152 | doi = 10.1070/RM2002v057n03ABEH000519 | mr = 1918864}}</ref> see Chapter XII of;<ref name = DDRW08/> the resulting algorithm admits a uniform complexity <math>O(\ell^2)</math>.

== Connection with knot theory ==
* Let <math>\Delta_n</math> be Garside's fundamental half-turn braid. Every braid <math>\beta</math> lies in a unique interval <math>[\Delta_n^{2m}, \Delta_n^{2m + 2})</math>; call the integer <math>m</math> the '''Dehornoy floor''' of <math>\beta</math>, denoted <math>\lfloor \beta \rfloor</math>. Then the link closure of braids with a large floor behave nicely, namely the properties of <math>\widehat{\beta}</math> can be read easily from <math>\beta</math>. Here are some examples.
* If <math>\vert \lfloor \beta \rfloor \vert > 1</math> then <math>\widehat{\beta}</math> is prime, non-split, and non-trivial.<ref>{{citation | last1 = Malyutin | first1 = Andrei | last2  = Netsvetaev | first2 = Nikita Yu. | title = Dehornoy order in the braid group and transformations of closed braids | journal = Rossiĭskaya Akademiya Nauk. Algebra i Analiz | date = 2003 | volume = 15 | number = 3 | pages = 170–187 | doi = 10.1090/S1061-0022-04-00816-7 | mr = 2052167| doi-access = free }}</ref>
* If <math>\vert \lfloor \beta \rfloor \vert > 1</math> and <math>\widehat{\beta}</math> is a knot, then <math>\widehat{\beta}</math> is a toric knot if and only if <math>\beta</math> is periodic, <math>\widehat{\beta}</math> is a [[satellite knot]] if and only if <math>\beta</math> is reducible, and <math>\widehat{\beta}</math> is hyperbolic if and only if <math>\beta</math> is pseudo-Anosov.<ref>{{citation | last = Ito | first = Tetsuya | title = Braid ordering and knot genus | journal = [[Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications]] | date = 2011 | volume = 20 | number = 9 | pages = 1311–1323 | doi = 10.1142/S0218216511009169 | mr = 2844810| arxiv = 0805.2042 | s2cid = 14609189 }}</ref>
